tasks.notes: Style, `skills/ultrawrite/SKILL.md` (rewritten §The proof gate dispatch paragraph): the second sentence opens `Dispatch it with the Agent tool, …` where the nearest antecedent for `it` is ambiguous — the preceding clause makes `Dispatch` a noun (`Dispatch is **per task**, not per round`), so `it` reads as either the dispatch or `every reader`. Naming the object keeps the rule unambiguous for the authoring agent that reads it, and no exam leg pins the pronoun (leg (c)'s sixth `Run:` only requires `Agent tool` in this paragraph), so the wording change is exam-neutral.

Prose/register (Global Constraint 1, whose `Check:` — three shouted words at zero — exited 0; this finding is my reading of the rule-with-its-reason register, not a failed check). The new reason clause reads "…without ever computing the number, where a reader asked exactly this computed six on the re-read…". `where` is used as a bare contrastive connective and `asked exactly this computed six` stacks two verbs with no relative pronoun, so the sentence that carries the rule's reason is the hardest sentence in §The proof gate to parse. The fix is a semicolon and one added word; it touches no literal any `Run:` greps (the first `Run:` cuts the section at `revised.`, before this clause) and leaves every line break intact, so the compile line stays on its own line for `tests/test_compile_plan_base_tree.py`. File: skills/ultrawrite/SKILL.md (§The proof gate, first paragraph).; unverified: the Acceptance line is `suite — the committed suite is the verification`, and no EXAM EVIDENCE was supplied — the committed suite was not shown executed on this tree. The Proof's four `Run:` commands and both constraint `Check:` commands are settled at exit 0, and I read the tests that pin the two regions this diff touches: `tests/test_compile_plan_integration_hostile.py` (species sentence, joined-section scope), `tests/test_compile_plan_base_tree.py` (compile line and the `--base` both-forms sentence), `tests/test_ultrawrite_surface_rules_implementer_check.py` (§Self-review's exam-file-naming line, shouted-word zeros), `tests/test_plan_level_claim.py` (§Self-review's `(derived)` / `plan-level Claim` tail) and `tests/test_ultrawrite_skill.py` (frontmatter/slot-order/validate) — none pins the rewritten first sentence, none requires the `**Closes:**` bullet to be §Self-review's last bullet, and no test caps the file's length, so all survive by inspection. A full `pytest tests/` run on this tree would settle it.
